h1: The 7 Best Room Divider Panels of 2026, Ranked & Reviewed
metaTitle: Best Room Divider Panels 2026: Ranked & Reviewed
metaDescription: Ranked and reviewed by Primea: 7 room divider panels scored on span, stability, fabric and portability, from RANTILA's 4-panel to rolling and modular models.
summary: The RANTILA 4-Panel Room Divider is the one to buy: 89 inches wide, 71 inches tall, triple-buckle hinges and wide foot pads for under $50. HOMSCREENER gives similar width with PA-coated fabric and 17.7 inch feet. SUNALLY adds lockable wheels for a divider you move often, VEVOR spans 136 inches, and DECOLAB is the permanent, fire-rated modular choice.
intro: A room divider fails in a very ordinary way: it falls over. Folding screens are tall, thin and lightweight, so the feet and hinges decide whether the divider stands or tips the first time someone brushes past. Width, panel count and fabric get the attention in product photos, but foot design is what keeps a screen upright in a real room.

We ranked seven panel dividers, from a single flexible panel to six-panel rolling screens and a modular fire-rated system, and scored them on the Primea framework. Stability and span carried the most weight, followed by fabric and construction, portability and price. Bookshelf dividers that double as storage were left out, since they solve a different problem and have their own guide.

products.name: RANTILA 4-Panel Room Divider with Wide Feet
products.verdict: 89 inches wide, 71 inches tall, triple-buckle hinges and extra-wide foot pads, under $50.
products.description:
RANTILA's four-panel divider is 89 inches wide and 71 inches tall, in 240gsm polyester over a steel frame. The hinges are triple-buckle, which locks adjacent panels firmly, and the extra-long, extra-wide foot pads widen the base, all at a price below $50.

It ranks first because it delivers the stability features that matter at the lowest price. Against HOMSCREENER, which costs more, it gives up the PA coating and water resistance but matches the width and panel count. The tradeoff is that fabric screens do little for sound: this blocks sight lines, not noise.

A strong choice for bedrooms, studios and shared offices where privacy is the goal. Keep it away from heavy traffic corners.
products.idealFor: Bedrooms and studios needing a stable, low-cost screen.

products.name: HOMSCREENER 4-Panel Fabric Privacy Screen
products.verdict: 88 inches of PA-coated fabric on 17.7 inch feet, wrinkle and water resistant.
products.description:
HOMSCREENER is 88 inches wide and 71.3 inches tall across four panels of 240gsm polyester on a steel frame, with a PA coating, triple-buckle hinges and extra-wide 17.7 inch feet. The fabric is wrinkle and water resistant.

It ranks just behind RANTILA because the specs are almost identical, and it costs more, in the $50 to $100 bracket. The PA coating is the justification: it sheds spills and resists creasing, which helps in damp spaces or near a kitchen. The 17.7 inch feet are stated, a figure RANTILA does not give.

Best for spaces where splashes or humidity are a concern. Otherwise RANTILA does the same job for less.
products.idealFor: Humid or splash-prone spaces needing a wipeable screen.
products.skipIf: You only need privacy and want the lowest price.

products.name: SUNALLY 6-Panel Room Divider with Lockable Wheels
products.verdict: 132 inches across six panels, on silent lockable wheels that let you roll it aside.
products.description:
SUNALLY stretches 132 inches wide and 72 inches tall across six panels of 240gsm polyester over steel, with silent PE lockable wheels, extended widened feet and wrinkle and water resistant fabric.

Wheels are the reason to buy it: rolling a six-panel screen across a floor is easier than lifting it, and the locks stop it drifting once placed. It ranks third because wheels add a trade: a wheeled base may be less planted than a fixed foot, and the six-panel width needs a large room. Compared with VEVOR, it is easier to reposition but spans 4 inches less.

A good fit for offices, studios and events where the divider moves often. Lock the wheels every time.
products.idealFor: Offices and studios where the divider is repositioned often.
products.skipIf: The divider will stay in one place in a small room.

products.name: VEVOR 4-Panel Folding Room Divider
products.verdict: 136 inches wide from four panels, in light-blocking waterproof Oxford fabric on an iron frame.
products.description:
VEVOR's four-panel divider is 136 inches wide and 72.4 inches tall, with Oxford fabric over an iron frame, light-blocking, waterproof fabric and W-shaped fold sections that give a stable zigzag.

With only four panels covering 136 inches, each panel is far wider than the 22 inch panels on RANTILA or HOMSCREENER, so the screen is bulkier to store and can feel less rigid. It ranks fourth because of that tradeoff, but nothing else here closes off a large open-plan room with so few joints. The light-blocking fabric also helps with privacy and glare.

A good fit for open-concept spaces and lofts. Measure the storage space before ordering.
products.idealFor: Open-concept rooms and lofts needing one continuous screen.
products.skipIf: You have limited storage or a small room.

products.name: MAYOLIAH 6-Panel Folding Privacy Screen
products.verdict: Reconfigures from 2 to 6 panels and spans up to 120 inches, with a 1-year warranty.
products.description:
MAYOLIAH lets you set between two and six panels for a span of up to 120 inches, 72 inches tall, in 180gsm polyester over an iron frame, with wider support feet and a 1-year warranty.

The adjustable width is the draw: if you are unsure how much room you need, you can fold away panels. It ranks fifth because the fabric is a lighter 180gsm than the 240gsm of RANTILA and SUNALLY, and the listing does not tout hinge design. The warranty is a useful extra, uncommon on fabric screens.

Good for renters who move and rearrange often. Check that the panels lock firmly when reconfigured.
products.idealFor: Renters who rearrange often and need a flexible width.

products.name: DECOLAB Standing Room Divider Panel
products.verdict: Magnetic modular panels with a fire-retardant, tackable surface and a 3-year warranty.
products.description:
DECOLAB sells 29 by 65 inch panels on a steel frame, covered in recyclable PET polyester that is flame retardant certified to CAL TB 117-2013 and tackable, with magnetic connections that let you add panels over time and a 3-year warranty.

It ranks sixth because it is the priciest, in the $100 to $200 bracket, and each panel is a single module, so a room-wide divider means buying several. What you get is a permanent install: the fire certification suits offices and shared spaces, and tackable fabric turns the screen into a pin board. Compared with RANTILA's folding screen, it is stationary and expandable.

A good pick for offices and classrooms. Home buyers will pay more than they need to.
cons: Each unit is a single module
products.idealFor: Offices and classrooms wanting a permanent, fire-rated divider.
products.skipIf: You want a cheap folding screen for a bedroom.

products.name: RANTILA Single Large Panel Room Divider
products.verdict: A single flexible UV-protected panel at 8.8 lb, 71 inches wide and waterproof.
products.description:
RANTILA's single large panel is a flexible HDPE sheet on a steel frame, 71 inches wide and 69.5 inches tall, with four internal stiffeners, UV protection and waterproofing. It weighs 8.8 lb.

It ranks last because a single sheet cannot fold into a zigzag, so stability depends on the frame alone and on the sheet staying taut. The listing does not cite feet or a hinge design. Against its sibling four-panel RANTILA, it is lighter and survives moisture, and even outdoors, but it spans far less and stands less firmly.

A fit for patios, porches or a corner where portability beats width. Anchor it against a wall.
products.idealFor: Patios, porches and quick, portable privacy.
products.skipIf: You need a wide, freestanding indoor divider.

methodology.title: Span and panel count
methodology.description: We compared total width and panel number, from a 71 inch single sheet to a 136 inch four-panel screen, against typical room openings.

methodology.title: Stability
methodology.description: Foot width, hinge design and wheels were weighed, because tipping is the most common failure of a freestanding screen.

methodology.title: Fabric and construction
methodology.description: Fabric weight from 180gsm to 240gsm, coatings, frame material and fire certification were compared.

methodology.title: Portability
methodology.description: Weight, wheels, foldability and reconfiguration were evaluated against how often the divider moves.

methodology.title: Value
methodology.description: Price brackets from under $50 to $200 were weighed against span and features.

whatMatters.detail: A tall folding screen balances on its feet, so wide, long feet resist tipping. The HOMSCREENER lists 17.7 inch feet. Look for extended or widened feet in the listing, and place the screen in a zigzag rather than straight, since a bent line braces itself.

More panels give more span and more stability when zigzagged, but also more storage bulk. Four panels of about 22 inches cover 88 inches, while the VEVOR's wide panels reach 136. Measure the opening, then divide by panel width to decide how many folds you need.

Fabric weight, in grams per square metre, indicates how opaque and durable a screen is. 240gsm polyester is heavier than 180gsm. A PA coating adds water resistance. Check the weight and any coating in the listing, and remember that fabric blocks sight, not sound.

Hinges decide how firmly panels hold their angle. Triple-buckle hinges lock panels more securely than single pivots. Look for hinge type in the listing, and test the screen by pushing gently from one end, since a good hinge will resist twisting rather than flopping.

Offices, classrooms and shared spaces often need fabric with a flame-retardant certification, such as CAL TB 117-2013 on the DECOLAB. Home bedrooms usually do not. Check your space's requirements before choosing, and look for the specific standard on the listing, not just the words flame retardant.

faq.q: Will a fabric room divider block sound?
faq.a: Barely. The RANTILA, HOMSCREENER and SUNALLY screens use polyester fabric that blocks sight lines. A heavier, thicker barrier would be needed for real noise reduction, so treat these as visual dividers.

faq.q: What mistake do buyers make with room dividers?
faq.a: Placing them in a straight line. A flat screen tips easily, while a zigzag braces itself. The VEVOR's W-shaped fold sections and the RANTILA's wide feet both depend on being set at angles.

faq.q: Is the DECOLAB worth it over a RANTILA?
faq.a: Only for offices or classrooms. The DECOLAB has fire-certified, tackable fabric and a 3-year warranty, but each 29 inch panel is a module, so a wide divider costs far more than the RANTILA 4-Panel.

faq.q: How do I set up a folding screen?
faq.a: Unfold it on a flat floor and zigzag the panels. On the SUNALLY, lock the wheels once positioned. For the RANTILA, spread the wide feet fully, and avoid pushing the end panel flat against traffic.

faq.q: How do I clean a divider?
faq.a: Wipe PA-coated fabric, as on the HOMSCREENER, with a damp cloth. Uncoated polyester like the RANTILA's needs a vacuum brush or gentle spot cleaning. The single RANTILA panel can be rinsed since it is waterproof.

faq.q: Can I use a divider outside?
faq.a: The RANTILA Single Large Panel is UV protected and waterproof, so it suits a patio or porch. Fabric screens such as the MAYOLIAH are better indoors, where sun and rain will not fade or soak them.

finalTake: For most rooms the RANTILA 4-Panel Room Divider is the right choice: an 89 inch span, triple-buckle hinges and wide feet for under $50. Choose HOMSCREENER for coated, wipeable fabric, SUNALLY if you need to roll it, and VEVOR for a very wide opening. The DECOLAB is for offices needing fire-rated panels.
